newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian mobile phone firm forecasts high growth.
newsitem.headline: Austrian mobile phone firm forecasts high growth.

text.p: Austria's only private mobile telephone company max.mobil said on Tuesday it was expecting meteoric growth this year and forecast it would snatch 50 percent of the growth in the market by 2000.

"The market is growing strongly so there is huge potential in the future. We expect to take 50 percent of the growth share by the end of the year 2000," chief executive Hansjoerg Tengg told a news conference.

Max.mobil, which was set up last year, currently has a 3.3 percent share of the mobile GSM market with some 30,000 subscribers. Tengg predicted that competitive pricing would drive the company's market share to 19.6 percent with 140,000 clients by the year end.
Max.mobil's business plan is to net 700,000 clients by the year 2,000.

Tengg said max.mobil is currently available to 60 percent of the Austrian population and that should rise to 90 percent by end of year as a result of the planned construction of 70 stations, which will bring the total to 1,100 by December.
Austria's biggest global system for mobile communications (GSM) network is dominated by Mobilkom, a unit of state monopoly Post und Telekom Austria (PTA), and has 400,000 clients.
